title: Reserve budgeting and eviction strategy for weights/KV/activation under continuous batching
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Problem: under mixed workloads (long-context chat + short requests + streaming) continuous batching and KV cache allocations compete with static weight residency and transient activations, causing occasional OOMs and noisy latency spikes. We need a unified budgeting model that maintains deterministic soft headroom for each GPU while minimizing wasted memory and preserving per-tenant latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc and simulation demonstrating <5% throughput loss at 99.9% OOM-free operation under benchmark mixed workload (chat + embeddings + short prompts).
Implementation that enforces a per-GPU reserve tiering policy (weights_reserved + kv_soft + activations_max) with runtime metrics exposed in Console (reserved vs used).
Automated tenant-level throttling/fallback path when soft headroom is breached without causing hard OOMs (graceful degradation).
Instrumentation and alerts: new metric gpu.memory.headroom_pct and alert when <7% for >30s; dashboard tile created in Console release runtime-1.26.
Integration tests that reproduce high-KV churn and validate eviction order and latency budgets across batching sizes (unit and e2e harness).
PRs merged, canary on Dedicated cluster for one week with zero customer regressions.
design_notes: New budgeting model splits GPU memory into three logical buckets: weights_pinned, kv_soft_reserve, activations_runtime_ceiling.
weights_pinned is computed from model artifact sizing + pinned quantized slabs; default targets are derived from model profile metadata in model catalog.

kv_soft_reserve is adaptive: base allocation = percentile(KV working set) over 1h; an elastic headroom factor (alpha) is learned online per-GPU using exponential smoothing to target OOM-rate <= target_oom (configurable, default 1e-5).

activations_runtime_ceiling uses request-level amortized estimates derived from sequence length distribution and batching window; continuous batching module must expose predicted activation delta to the allocator before commit.

Eviction policy: multi-tier FIFO/LRU hybrid — prefer evicting non-pinned, cold KV segments first; when kv_soft_reserve exhausted, trigger tenant-level degradation (shorten max_context, switch to quantized KV variant), not immediate weight offload.
Hard reserve: a minimum weight residency and GPU-critical kernel buffers cannot be reclaimed; allocator must never allow reclaim below this hard floor.
Policy configurability: per-tenant weight priority, SLA tag (low/standard/premium) that influences kv_soft_reserve elasticity and allowed degradation steps.

Safety nets: background sampler that simulates headroom under current workload to produce recommended alpha adjustments; outputs stored as telemetry for offline analysis and included in Optimize suggestions.

Trade-offs: more conservative headroom reduces OOM risk but increases idle memory and reduces throughput economics; learning alpha reduces manual tuning but increases complexity and potential feedback loops — mitigations include rate-limiting alpha updates and sanity clamps.
Compatibility: design must integrate with existing KV cache format and not require model recompile; new alloc APIs introduced are backward-compatible shims that default to legacy behavior.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + simulation, 1 week): build micro-simulator to replay MixedWorkload traces (from perf lab) and validate candidate alpha schedules. Deliver design + simulation results.

Phase 2 (allocator + telemetry, 2 weeks): add reserve accounting to GPU allocator, expose gpu.memory.headroom_pct and per-tenant kv_reserve_used metrics; implement eviction hooks for KV cold-first policy.
Phase 3 (batcher integration, 1 week): make continuous-batcher query predicted activation delta before commit; batcher to optionally reduce batch size when headroom low.
Phase 4 (policy & learning, 2 weeks): implement online alpha learner with rate limits and clamps; add per-SLA policy layer to decide degradation actions.
Phase 5 (tests + canary, 1 week): unit + e2e tests; deploy canary to dedicated cluster and monitor metrics/alerts. Rollout if stable.
Owner: Ravi Patel. Reviewers: Mei Chen (serving-runtime), Carlos Ruiz (observability), Priya Natarajan (SRE).
testing_and_metrics: Create mixed_workload_v2 trace (20k requests, 60% chat long-context, 30% short prompts, 10% embeddings) — baseline: current allocator with no soft reserve learning.
Run A/B with new allocator: compare 95th and 99th latency, OOM count, GPU utilization, and token cost deltas over 6h windows.
Key metrics to monitor: gpu.memory.headroom_pct, kv_cache.evictions.rate, requests.throttled.count, tenant.latency_p99, oom.count (per-host).
Failure injection: artificially force sudden KV churn (hot key storms) and ensure fallback degradation executes and avoids OOMs while preserving premium tenant SLA.
E2E regression suite to run nightly against runtime-1.26 images.
SLO target: keep OOMs <= 1 per 1M requests on canary clusters; latency regressions <= 5% for standard SLA tenants.
